component.name: Oscyl
component.summary: Library, sound editor and sync for the minilogue xd

description.p: Oscyl manages the programs of a KORG minilogue xd synthesiser. Browse, organise and edit libraries offline, with no synth attached; every parameter has its own control. With the synth connected over USB, you can audition edits live before storing them.

Sync writes only the programs that changed, and before it writes Oscyl shows exactly which slots will change. A built-in simulated synth lets you try sync and audition without hardware. Oscyl is an independent open-source project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by KORG.
Oscyl finds a minilogue xd on Windows and installs there for your user, Hold to compare keeps your notes sounding, and the documentation is a book that starts from zero.
Generate goes deeper and uses the units in your synth, Oscyl makes oscillators of its own for logue synths, the desktop app shares the phone app's look, and it now runs on Windows and macOS too.
Android app, an iOS app ready for its first build, and two more synths: the KORG prologue and the Sequential Prophet Rev2. Several synths at once, Generate, and safer libraries in Oscyl's own format.
Redesigned editor: one chart band with a single signal line through six stages, live graphs you can drag, and a backup of the slots a sync replaces.
Development snapshot of the GNOME app (library manager, sound editor and sync), with an app icon, desktop entry and Flatpak manifest.
